To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the molecular recognition templates of dipeptide substrats of dipeptide permeases and dipeptidase enzymes are defined by a combination of electronic, conformational, and structural features of the substrates.

dipeptides are transported by peptide transporters in a substrate-specific manner, that substrate specificity arises from the complement of conformers that a peptide adopts in solution and that this complement defines the molecular recognition template (MRT) that is recognized by each transporter.

the molecular recognition templates of peptide transporters and dipeptidase enzymes are similar, and that these MRTs provide a basis for the rational design and synthesis of peptide-based drugs that exploit these peptide transporters and enzymes in microorganisms and humans.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of molecular recognition templates for the recognition of peptides and peptidomimetics by transport proteins, and with the application of this information in the development of peptide-based drugs.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
peptide transporters and peptide hydrolases are highly selective for dipeptides that have particular conformations and electronic properties, which can be predicted by computational methods.
the structural basis for molecular recognition of dipeptide substrats by peptide transporters can be defined in terms of the repertoire of conformations adopted by the dipeptides in aqueous solution.

peptide transporters and dipeptidase enzymes are highly specific for the conformers adopted by the substrates, and this specificity is determined by the electronic and conformational characteristics of the substrates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the molecular recognition of dipeptide substrats by peptide transporters can be defined by a set of structural and electronic criteria.
the MRTs for the peptide substrates of the dipeptidase and dipeptide permeases are defined by the presence of a single hydrogen bond acceptor and one or two hydrogen bond donors in the dipeptide.
we have identified the molecular recognition templates of the peptide transporters, and that these are likely to be similar for dipeptidase enzymes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular recognition of peptide substrates by peptide transporters is a highly specific process that is governed by strict structural and electronic requirements.
the molecular recognition template (MRT) of a substrate by its transporter can be identified from the repertoire of conformations that it adopts in solution.
a peptide is recognized by a protein as a substrate only if its repertoire of conformers includes one or more that match the MRT of the protein.
